scenarios.note: SessionStart with cwd inside ${CODEX_HOME}/worktrees/<slot>/<repo> that has a .git entry: WORKTREE-GUARD-01 identity context naming checkout, slot and root with the ADOPT IN PLACE advice; no marker is written.
Managed slot without any .git entry up to the slot root: still managed, but the checkout is reported as unconfirmed and the git-branch advice is replaced by the plain stay-and-commit line.
CODEXCLAW_WORKTREE_ROOTS (':'-separated, first entry unused) adds a root outside CODEX_HOME; a checkout under it is managed with its own slot.
Not managed: the workspace, the worktrees root itself, and a managed-looking path when CODEX_HOME points elsewhere. All three print nothing.
A workspace symlink pointing into the managed checkout is canonicalised: the context names the real slot paths while echoing the symlinked cwd.
The worktree context legs are not in the PABCD-disabled set: CODEXCLAW_PABCD=off still injects. A subagent-stamped payload (agent_id) hits the root-only early exit and is silent.

Korean rename intent on a managed worktree injects WORKTREE-GUARD-02 and writes the once-per-session marker <cwd>/.codexclaw/worktree-guard/<session>.json; the same session asking again (English) is silent; a new session gets the guidance again.
No rename intent (only one of the two regexes matches, or neither) on a managed cwd, and rename intent on an unmanaged cwd: silent, no marker.
WORKTREE-GUARD-03: `git worktree remove` of the session's own checkout (plain, --force, via git -C) and of its slot root are each denied with the PreToolUse deny envelope.
rm/rmdir variants on the protected tree: sudo/env/command prefixes, /bin/rm -rf . from the checkout, long flags, `--`, rmdir, a `cd` compound, and `rm -rf ..` (ancestor of cwd). Every step denies.
Conservative fallback: a destructive op whose target does not resolve ($X) while the raw command mentions the slot id denies with the 'unresolvable target' reason.
Oracle quirk pinned: the fallback matches the slot id as a raw substring, so `rm -rf ./build-7627` (an unrelated child directory) is denied as an unresolvable target, while `rm -rf ./build` passes.
Benign and out-of-scope commands on a managed cwd pass silently: git status, worktree list/prune, removing another worktree, a non-recursive rm, unlink of a file, ls.
The deletion guard is dispatched above the subagent early exit (audit B3): a payload stamped with agent_id/agent_type is still denied.
Fail-open paths: rm -rf of an unmanaged workspace, a non-Bash tool name, a Bash call without command, a non-PreToolUse event and malformed JSON all print nothing.
Protection follows detection: a checkout under CODEXCLAW_WORKTREE_ROOTS is protected, and a symlinked workspace path into the managed checkout is canonicalised so `rm -rf .` there denies.

MEMORY-WRITE-GATE-01: a memory-tool write with no prompt marker and no CLI grant is denied; the reason names the note, the session id and the cwd. Punctuated tool-name variants of the matcher are classified the same.
A 'Remember this:' prompt through the PABCD trigger leg records memoryWriteRequested for the turn; the next memory write in that turn passes and consumes it; a second write is denied.

stdin.prompt: Remember this: the staging host is called blue.

scenarios.note: The prompt marker belongs to its turn: a write attributed to another turn is denied and does not consume it; the asking turn still passes.

`cxc memory allow-write --session rec-s1` from the workspace records memoryWriteGrant and prints the cwd it wrote; the next memory write passes and spends it; the one after is denied.
The --session=<id> spelling through the repository dispatcher, and the same verb through the plugin's own bin/cxc.mjs; both record the grant in the workspace session file.
Parse errors exit 2 with `memory: <error>` plus usage on stderr and write nothing: a non-canonical session id, a missing --session, an unknown flag.
--help anywhere in allow-write prints usage, exits 0 and records no grant, so the following memory write is still denied.

Advisory silent: Codex config not full access (workspace-write), permission_mode full-access, agent_type present, a user-thread rollout, a broken rollout line, and a non-string cwd.
